svg.text: A visual comparison of data distribution, fault tolerance, and redundancy mechanisms
Combines mirroring and striping. Provides the high performance of RAID 0 alongside the high fault tolerance of RAID 1.
Combines multiple drives sequentially into a single logical volume. No striping,no parity, and no performance gain.
Uses two independent parity blocks distributed across all disks. Can withstand two simultaneous drive failures.
Stripes data across drives along with distributed parity info.Balanced performance and capacity efficiency.
Data is split evenly across two or more drives.Offers high performance but zero protection; a single drive failure destroys all data.
Creates an identical copy of data on two or more disks. Excellent read speed and high redundancy, but usable capacity is cut in half.
